narrative:
The model determined that you have a 51% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is just over the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the type of property you own. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. Only 12.6% of approved applicants are in this situation, while most (59%) have no checking account or a positive balance. This signaled higher risk to the model.

Your credit history of “no credits or all paid” was the second most important driver and also pushed the outcome toward denial. This is quite rare—only 1% of approved applicants share this history—whereas the large majority (57%) have a record of existing credits that were paid on time.

The one positive element was that you own real estate. This worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval, but unfortunately it was not enough to overcome the concerns from your account status and credit history.

You should focus on building a stronger credit history by taking out and reliably repaying small loans or credit cards over time, and by bringing your checking account balance into positive territory. Once these areas improve, reapply and your chances of approval should increase significantly. (218 words)
